chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God have mercy on him - narrated that Al-Hasan ibn Matil al-Daq'qaq quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Awf al-Ajli, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
Washing (the hands) before and after food increases one's provision.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الرِّزْقِ: Provision, sustenance, or livelihood granted by God.
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: Ritual ablution or washing, specifically here referring to washing hands before and after meals.

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of performing wudu before and after eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration linking ritual purity to sustenance, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnection between physical cleanliness and spiritual well-being. This practice is viewed not merely as hygiene but as a means of attracting divine favor, aligning with the broader theological concept that obedience and purity open the gates of *rizq*. The Imam’s statement underscores the transformative power of small, consistent acts of worship in daily life.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-82 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God forgive him - narrated that Al-Hassan ibn Matil al-Daq’qaq quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil-Khat’tab, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Abi Oaf al-Ajali that he had heard Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say, “
Washing hands before and after every meal will increase your share of daily bread.”
